articles.title: Inside Health - Cardio vs strength training: which is better? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Plus, a new study measuring levels of forever chemicals in our blood launches in the UK.
articles.body: The UK Health Security Agency has launched a major study to find out what level of forever chemicals the average person in the UK has in their bodies. With results not expected until 2027, we speak to the UKHSA’s Dr Edward Wynne-Evans and Professor Tony Fletcher from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine about what is and is not known about per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and their potential impacts on our health. And, with the help of Damian Bailey, professor of physiology and biochemistry at the University of South Wales, Laura hits the gym to work out if more of us are ditching cardio and aerobic exercise in favour of strength training, what that could mean for our health decades down the line. Then with fines set to be introduced on buses for people playing music and videos out loud on their phones, we look at whether spending more of our lives wearing headphones and earphones is changing not just what we hear, but how we hear. Presenter: Laura Foster Producer: Imogen Harper Assistant Producer: Tabitha Taylor Buck Editor: Ilan Goodman Sound engineer: Tim Heffer Production coordinator: Stu Laws The show was made by the BBC Audio's Science Unit in collaboration with The Open University.

articles.title: Riscos psicossociais: como avaliar além da pesquisa de clima | G1
articles.standfirst: Conformidade exige compreender o trabalho real, combinar evidências e transformar o diagnóstico em inventário, prioridades e ações acompanhadas.
articles.summary: Conformidade exige compreender o trabalho real, combinar evidências e transformar o diagnóstico em inventário, prioridades e ações acompanhadas.
articles.body:
Riscos psicossociais: como avaliar além da pesquisa de clima — Foto: Crédito: Corpmed.

Uma pesquisa de clima pode revelar percepções importantes sobre liderança, comunicação e satisfação. Mas ela não responde, sozinha, às exigências de gerenciamento dos fatores de risco psicossociais relacionados ao trabalho. Desde 26 de maio de 2026, a nova redação do capítulo 1.5 da NR-1 exige que esses fatores sejam considerados no Gerenciamento de Riscos Ocupacionais, o GRO.

A diferença é prática: clima organizacional descreve como as pessoas percebem o ambiente em determinado momento; avaliação de risco investiga perigos e fatores presentes na organização e na gestão do trabalho, estima riscos, define prioridades e sustenta medidas de prevenção. Um bom índice de satisfação não elimina, por exemplo, jornadas excessivas, metas incompatíveis, baixa autonomia, conflitos de papel, assédio ou falta de apoio.

O que a NR-1 exige — e o que ela não padroniza

A obrigação legal é incluir os fatores de risco psicossociais relacionados ao trabalho no processo do GRO, registrá-los no inventário quando identificados, avaliar os riscos, estabelecer medidas no plano de ação e acompanhar sua implementação e eficácia. A organização também deve assegurar mecanismos de participação dos trabalhadores e comunicar os riscos e as medidas de prevenção.

A norma não transforma um questionário específico em requisito universal nem estabelece uma plataforma única. A técnica deve ser adequada ao perigo, ao perfil da população, às atividades e à complexidade da empresa. Questionários podem integrar o processo, mas o resultado precisa ser analisado à luz do trabalho real e conectado ao inventário e ao plano de ação.

Aplicar uma pesquisa é uma atividade. Gerenciar riscos é um ciclo: identificar, avaliar, controlar, registrar, acompanhar e rever com participação dos trabalhadores.

Por que um único número pode esconder o risco

Médias corporativas misturam realidades diferentes. Uma organização pode apresentar resultado global favorável e, ao mesmo tempo, ter uma equipe com sobrecarga, uma unidade exposta à violência ou um turno com baixa previsibilidade. Recortes muito pequenos, por outro lado, podem identificar pessoas e comprometer a confiança. A análise exige equilíbrio entre capacidade de localizar o problema e proteção da confidencialidade.

A taxa de resposta também importa. Baixa adesão, medo de retaliação, dificuldade de acesso digital ou aplicação durante período atípico podem distorcer a leitura. Resultado estatístico não deve ser interpretado sem observar contexto, distribuição das respostas, diferenças entre grupos e informações qualitativas.

Avaliação multimétodo: evidências que se complementam

Não existe uma combinação idêntica para todas as empresas. Conforme o caso, a avaliação pode reunir análise documental, observação da atividade, entrevistas, grupos de escuta, questionários validados, dados agregados de saúde e afastamentos, informações sobre jornada, horas extras, rotatividade, incidentes, queixas, mudanças organizacionais e canais de denúncia.

Instrumentos voltados às condições psicossociais do trabalho podem ajudar a organizar dimensões como demandas, controle, apoio, relações, papel e mudanças. Já instrumentos de rastreamento de sofrimento mental, como o SRQ-20, têm finalidade diferente: podem apoiar vigilância de saúde quando tecnicamente indicados, mas não diagnosticam individualmente nem substituem a avaliação dos fatores presentes no trabalho.

O uso de qualquer ferramenta exige finalidade definida, qualificação técnica, comunicação transparente, proteção de dados e interpretação responsável. Dados de saúde são dados pessoais sensíveis pela LGPD. Lideranças devem receber tendências e recomendações agregadas, não respostas individuais ou hipóteses diagnósticas.

Definir o escopo: mapear unidades, atividades, turnos, mudanças recentes, populações e situações críticas que precisam ser compreendidas.

Preparar a governança: definir responsáveis, participação de SST, RH, Saúde, Jurídico, Operações e trabalhadores, além de regras de confidencialidade e comunicação.

Reconhecer o trabalho real: observar como metas, recursos, autonomia, jornada, relações e imprevistos afetam a execução da atividade.

Combinar métodos: selecionar entrevistas, grupos, questionários, documentos e indicadores apropriados ao contexto, sem aplicar ferramentas por automatismo.

Analisar por fatores: distinguir perigos, grupos expostos, controles existentes, gravidade possível, probabilidade e incertezas da avaliação.

Validar os achados: devolver resultados de forma agregada e verificar com trabalhadores e gestores se a interpretação representa a realidade.

Integrar ao PGR: registrar os fatores pertinentes no inventário e converter prioridades em medidas, responsáveis, prazos e critérios de acompanhamento.

Monitorar: acompanhar implantação e eficácia, rever riscos após mudanças e manter canais capazes de detectar novas situações.

A ação deve alcançar a organização do trabalho

Palestras, apoio psicológico, práticas de relaxamento e programas de bem-estar podem ter valor como medidas complementares. Entretanto, não controlam por si só fatores como dimensionamento insuficiente, metas contraditórias, falta de autonomia, violência, assédio ou jornadas inadequadas. A prevenção primária busca modificar a fonte do risco sempre que tecnicamente possível.

A Fundacentro ressalta a importância de analisar condições, organização e gestão do trabalho com participação efetiva dos trabalhadores, evitando explicações que individualizam o adoecimento. Isso não significa atribuir automaticamente toda condição de saúde ao trabalho; significa investigar de forma estruturada quais características do trabalho podem contribuir para o risco.

A Corpmed estrutura a avaliação psicossocial de acordo com porte, atividades, dispersão geográfica, riscos, histórico, maturidade e capacidade de intervenção de cada organização. Em alguns casos, o ponto de partida será um levantamento quantitativo amplo; em outros, a prioridade pode ser observar uma atividade crítica, ouvir determinados grupos ou investigar mudanças recentes.

O valor da metodologia não está em gerar um selo ou uma nota isolada. Está em produzir evidências rastreáveis, proteger as pessoas, localizar prioridades e orientar decisões que possam ser implementadas e acompanhadas por RH, SST, Saúde, Jurídico, Operações e liderança.

SUA AVALIAÇÃO PSICOSSOCIAL MOSTRA O QUE PRECISA MUDAR?

Conheça a metodologia da Corpmed para avaliar fatores psicossociais conforme o contexto de cada empresa e integrá-los ao PGR.

Desde 2006, a Corpmed atua em saúde e segurança ocupacional com equipe multidisciplinar de mais de 30 profissionais, operação centralizada em Campinas e atendimento nacional por rede credenciada. Seu modelo integra gestão médica, SST, RH, Jurídico e Operações com suporte contínuo, rastreabilidade e uso de dados.

articles.title: Peixe-leão na Bahia: espécie invasora e venenosa é vista em Itacaré | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal foi identificado por pescadores em Itacaré; prefeitura orienta população a não tocar no peixe e comunicar avistamentos ao Inema.
articles.summary: Identificado por pescadores em Itacaré, o peixe-leão na Bahia alerta para riscos de acidentes com veneno e danos à biodiversidade marinha no litoral sul do estado.
articles.body:
Peixe-leão, espécie invasora com veneno capaz de causar acidentes, é encontrado no litoral da Bahia — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Um exemplar de peixe-leão, espécie invasora que possui espinhos venenosos e pode provocar acidentes, foi encontrado no litoral de Itacaré , no sul da Bahia. O animal foi identificado por pescadores locais na segunda-feira (2), segundo informou a Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente.

Originário da região do Indo-Pacífico, o peixe-leão é considerado uma espécie exótica invasora. Nos últimos anos, ele tem ampliado sua presença no Oceano Atlântico e já foi registrado em diferentes pontos da costa brasileira.

🔍 ENTENDA: como está fora de sua área de distribuição natural, esse peixe venenoso pode provocar impactos na biodiversidade ao predar outras espécies e alterar o equilíbrio dos ecossistemas recifais.

A presença do animal preocupa por dois motivos: o risco de acidentes com pessoas e os possíveis impactos sobre a biodiversidade marinha.

O peixe-leão é um predador de diversas espécies de peixes e crustáceos. Por não ser nativo da região, sua presença pode desequilibrar os ecossistemas marinhos e afetar outras espécies.

Além dos impactos ambientais, o animal oferece riscos para quem entra em contato com ele. Seus espinhos possuem veneno, que pode provocar dor intensa e febre. Em situações mais graves, o contato também pode causar convulsões.

Por isso, a Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente orienta pescadores, trabalhadores do mar, operadores de turismo e moradores a não tocar ou tentar manipular o peixe-leão.

Em caso de avistamento ou captura do animal, a orientação é comunicar o Instituto do Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (Inema), responsável por receber as informações e orientar sobre os procedimentos adequados. O contato pode ser feito pelo telefone ou WhatsApp: (71) 99671-3998.

Sempre que possível, também é importante registrar:

O horário em que o animal foi encontrado.

As informações ajudam os órgãos ambientais a monitorar a presença da espécie e acompanhar sua distribuição pelo litoral baiano.

articles.title: Tráfico de drogas em Macapá: Padrasto e enteado são presos | G1
articles.standfirst: Dois suspeitos foram presos nesta segunda-feira (2), no bairro do Buritizal. Eles são investigados em uma operação que já cumpriu 11 mandados contra uma organização criminosa que atua no interior do estado.
articles.summary: Tráfico de drogas em Macapá motiva a prisão de padrasto e enteado durante a Operação Interstício, que investiga grupo criminoso com atuação no interior do estado.
articles.body:
Um homem de 23 anos e o padrasto dele, de 41, foram presos nesta segunda-feira (2), no bairro Buritizal, na Zona Sul de Macapá , durante uma ação ligada à Operação Intestício. Segundo a polícia, os dois são suspeitos de envolvimento com o tráfico de drogas e integrariam uma facção criminosa investigada no Amapá .

A prisão ocorreu durante o cumprimento de mandados relacionados à operação, que já resultou em 11 ordens judiciais contra suspeitos de integrar um grupo criminoso com atuação no município de Ferreira Gomes.

De acordo com a polícia, os dois homens foram autuados em flagrante por crimes relacionados ao tráfico de drogas, associação para o tráfico, posse e porte ilegal de arma de fogo e participação em organização criminosa.

Durante as buscas, os agentes apreenderam porções de drogas e materiais que, segundo a investigação, seriam utilizados para o armazenamento e a comercialização dos entorpecentes.

Padrasto e enteado são presos em flagrante em Macapá — Foto: Polícia Civil/Divulgação

Após a prisão, os suspeitos foram encaminhados ao Centro Integrado de Operações em Segurança Pública (Ciosp) do Pacoval, onde permanecem à disposição da Justiça.

Eles devem passar por audiência de custódia nos próximos dias.

articles.title: Entregador implora para não ter moto roubada em Belém; veja vídeo | G1
articles.standfirst: Tentativa de assalto ocorreu na noite de segunda-feira 2, no cruzamento do canal da Pirajá com a travessa Doutor Freitas, no bairro da Pedreira.
articles.summary: Câmeras registraram o momento em que um entregador implora para não ter a moto roubada durante uma tentativa de assalto no bairro da Pedreira, em Belém.
articles.body:
Um entregador por aplicativo viveu momentos de tensão na noite desta segunda-feira (2), após ser abordado por um homem que tentou roubar sua motocicleta, no bairro da Pedreira, em Belém - veja no vídeo acima.

Uma câmera de segurança registrou a abordagem, o caso ocorreu por volta das 22h. Nas imagens, o entregador aparece ao lado da motocicleta enquanto é confrontado por um homem.

Em meio à situação, ele chega a se ajoelhar e implorar para não ter o veículo levado. O suspeito permanece próximo à moto por alguns instantes e depois deixa o local a pé.

Após a saída do suspeito, o trabalhador volta a subir na motocicleta e deixa o local.

O g1 entrou em contato com as Polícias Civil e Militar solicitando um posicionamento sobre o caso, mas ainda não obteve retorno até a última atualização da reportagem.

articles.title: Aulão na Rede 2026: professor explica conceitos de Biotecnologia   | G1
articles.standfirst: Videoaula está disponível para estudantes que se preparam para o Enem, vestibulares e outras avaliações.
articles.summary: Videoaula está disponível para estudantes que se preparam para o Enem, vestibulares e outras avaliações.
articles.body:
Diariamente, os telejornais da Rede Amazônica disponibilizam videoaulas do projeto "Aulão na Rede". Nesta terça-feira (3), o professor Mário Silva, explicou sobre Biotecnologia. O conteúdo está disponível para estudantes que se preparam para o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio ( Enem ), vestibulares e outras avaliações. (veja vídeo acima)

A iniciativa reúne videoaulas exibidas diariamente nos telejornais da Rede Amazônica , com orientações de professores de diferentes áreas do conhecimento para auxiliar os candidatos na reta final de preparação.

Durante a aula, o professor Mário Silva, explica que a engenharia genética e a biotecnologia vêm transformando diferentes setores da sociedade ao permitir a manipulação do DNA, molécula responsável por armazenar as informações genéticas dos seres vivos. Ele destacou que essas técnicas possibilitam avanços importantes na agricultura, na pecuária e na medicina, contribuindo para o aumento da produtividade, o desenvolvimento de organismos mais resistentes e a criação de tratamentos inovadores para diversas doenças.

Segundo a explicação, a engenharia genética resulta da integração entre conhecimentos da biologia e da engenharia, utilizando laboratórios especializados e tecnologias avançadas para alterar características genéticas de organismos.

Os vídeos do projeto "Aulão na Rede" ficam disponíveis gratuitamente e abordam temas recorrentes nas provas do Enem e de vestibulares.

articles.title: Menopausa muito além do calorão: sinais que nem sempre são reconhecidos | G1
articles.standfirst: Mudanças no sono, na libido e no humor podem marcar essa transição. Em Santos, a Solle Saúde reúne uma equipe multidisciplinar para cuidar da longevidade feminina.
articles.summary: Mudanças no sono, na libido e no humor podem marcar essa transição. Em Santos, a Solle Saúde reúne uma equipe multidisciplinar para cuidar da longevidade feminina.
articles.body:
Clínica Solle Saúde Santos/SP — Foto: Lumify

O calorão costuma ser o primeiro sintoma lembrado quando o assunto é menopausa. Mas, para muitas mulheres, as mudanças aparecem de outras formas: noites mal dormidas, dificuldade de concentração, alterações no desejo sexual e uma disposição que já não acompanha a rotina. Sem reconhecer essa relação, algumas seguem atribuindo tudo ao estresse ou ao excesso de responsabilidades.

A transição para a menopausa pode afetar o bem-estar físico, emocional e social. Os sintomas e sua intensidade variam de uma mulher para outra, o que torna importante compreender a experiência individual e investigar o que está interferindo na qualidade de vida.

As mudanças podem começar antes da última menstruação

A menopausa é confirmada após 12 meses consecutivos sem menstruar, quando não há outra causa para essa ausência. Antes disso, a perimenopausa pode trazer oscilações hormonais, irregularidade no ciclo e sintomas que nem sempre são identificados como parte dessa transição.

Alterações de humor, ansiedade, dificuldades de memória e concentração estão entre as manifestações possíveis. Como essas queixas também podem ter outras causas, o acompanhamento ajuda a entender o quadro sem atribuir automaticamente todo desconforto aos hormônios.

Na Solle Saúde, a longevidade feminina é acompanhada por uma equipe multidisciplinar. A proposta é conectar avaliação médica, acompanhamento nutricional e outros cuidados indicados a partir das necessidades de cada paciente.

Uma mulher que procura atendimento por cansaço, por exemplo, pode precisar conversar também sobre alimentação, sono, rotina e saúde emocional. Reunir essas informações permite definir prioridades e construir um plano de cuidado que possa ser acompanhado e ajustado ao longo do tempo.

“Quando uma mulher diz que não se reconhece mais no próprio corpo ou que perdeu a disposição, precisamos acolher e investigar essa queixa. O cuidado com a longevidade feminina envolve olhar para o sono, a alimentação, a sexualidade, a saúde emocional e as mudanças hormonais. A equipe multidisciplinar ajuda a conectar essas necessidades”, explica Priscilla Sartori, CRF: 53718, que atua no cuidado da longevidade feminina na Solle Saúde.

Libido e autoestima também entram nessa conversa

Ressecamento vaginal, desconforto nas relações e mudanças no desejo sexual podem aparecer nessa fase. A sexualidade também é influenciada por fatores como estresse, medicamentos, sono e relacionamento. Por isso, falar sobre essas questões durante a consulta abre espaço para avaliar as causas e as possibilidades de tratamento.

Perceber mudanças na intimidade e na aparência pode afetar a confiança e a relação com o próprio corpo. No atendimento, essas experiências merecem espaço, sem constrangimento. O objetivo é compreender o que incomoda aquela mulher e quais aspectos ela deseja cuidar.

Nutrição e necessidades de reposição merecem avaliação

A atenção à alimentação também faz parte do cuidado nessa etapa. Cálcio e vitamina D são importantes para a saúde óssea, e as recomendações de ingestão de cálcio aumentam para mulheres a partir dos 51 anos. Isso reforça a necessidade de avaliar se a alimentação está atendendo às demandas individuais.

Na Solle, o acompanhamento nutricional integra essa avaliação, considerando hábitos, dificuldades da rotina e necessidades específicas. Quando indicada, a investigação de deficiências pode orientar a reposição de vitaminas e minerais, com acompanhamento profissional.

A suplementação deve responder a uma necessidade identificada. Ela compõe o plano de cuidado quando apropriada, junto da alimentação e das demais condutas definidas pela equipe.

Metabolismo, músculos e saúde ao longo dos anos

As mudanças na composição corporal também merecem atenção. A redução do estrogênio pode favorecer o acúmulo de gordura abdominal, enquanto envelhecimento, perda de massa muscular, sono e nível de atividade física participam das alterações de peso.

Por isso, acompanhar a saúde nessa fase envolve mais do que observar a balança. Preservar força, avaliar a saúde metabólica e construir hábitos sustentáveis são aspectos relevantes para a autonomia e o bem-estar nos próximos anos.

O tratamento dos sintomas pode incluir medidas hormonais ou não hormonais, conforme histórico clínico, preferências e avaliação individual de benefícios e riscos. Não existe uma única conduta adequada para todas as mulheres.

A menopausa também pode abrir espaço para recomeços

Retomar projetos, rever prioridades ou reservar mais tempo para si são possibilidades que podem acompanhar essa etapa. Cada mulher tem seu ritmo, e o cuidado deve respeitar tanto suas dificuldades quanto seus objetivos.

Em Santos, a Solle Saúde reúne diferentes profissionais para apoiar esse percurso. Com avaliação e acompanhamento multidisciplinar, a clínica conecta o cuidado dos sintomas à alimentação, à saúde emocional e à construção da longevidade feminina.

articles.title: Ladrões invadem escola municipal em Sertãozinho, SP, e furtam torneira | G1
articles.standfirst: EMEI Maria Ignez Faneco Pignata funciona normalmente, já que os suspeitos não danificaram as salas de aulas.
articles.summary: EMEI Maria Ignez Faneco Pignata funciona normalmente, já que os suspeitos não danificaram as salas de aulas.
articles.body:
Ladrões furtaram torneiras e danificaram computadores da EMEI Maria Ignez Faneco Pignata, em Sertãozinho, SP — Foto: Divulgação/GCM de Sertãozinho, SP

Uma escola municipal em Sertãozinho (SP) foi alvo de criminosos, que invadiram o local na madrugada desta terça-feira (3) para furtar dinheiro, torneiras e um celular.

De acordo com a Secretaria Municipal de Educação, a EMEI Maria Ignez Faneco Pignata funciona normalmente, já que os suspeitos não danificaram as salas de aulas. A escola fica no Jardim Alvorada.

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Sertãozinho informou que as torneiras foram substituídas pela equipe da Secretaria Obras, Conservação e Serviços Públicos ainda pela manhã.

A Guarda Civil Municipal (GCM) esteve no local após receber uma denúncia de invasão por volta da 1h da manhã e constatou que os diversos cômodos foram revirados e computadores foram danificados e quebrados. A Prefeitura de Sertãozinho informou que foram levados R$ 500.

"Ao realizar a vistoria do local, a corporação identificou atos de vandalismo na ala administrativa, bem como furto de 15 torneiras do pátio, além de um celular e uma quantia de R$ 500 pertencentes à escola. A GCM registrou a ocorrência e está trabalhando na tentativa de identificar os autores".

articles.title: Vídeo: carro com família capota após bater contra outros três veículos | G1
articles.standfirst: Veículo estava com a documentação regular e foi retirado da pista por um guincho particular.
articles.summary: Veículo estava com a documentação regular e foi retirado da pista por um guincho particular.
articles.body:
Um motorista foi levado ao hospital após o carro que ele dirigia capotar depois de bater contra outros três veículos na Avenida Fernando Corrêa da Costa, em Cuiabá , na manhã desta terça-feira (3). A esposa do motorista, que está grávida, e a filha do casal, de 4 anos, também estavam no carro, mas não se feriram.

Imagens registradas pela equipe da TV Centro América mostram o veículo capotado no meio da pista (veja acima) .

Familiares informaram que o motorista chegou a desmaiar após o acidente, mas recobrou a consciência e foi levado ao hospital com um corte na boca . O estado de saúde dele é considerado estável.

Carro capotado em meio a Avenida Fernando Corrêa da Costa, em Cuiabá — Foto: Reprodução

A retirada do carro, que está com documentação regular, foi feita por um guincho particular. Os ocupantes dos outros três veículos não se feriram e tiveram apenas danos materiais.

A Secretaria de Mobilidade Urbana (Semob) fez o controle do trânsito, que já foi liberado e flui normalmente. A causa do acidente ainda deve ser investigada.

articles.title: Ouriço-cacheiro surpreende moradores em espelho de banheiro em MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal silvestre foi resgatado em Muriaé. Moradores suspeitam que o ouriço tenha atravessado a proteção de tela da janela para entrar na casa.
articles.summary: Corpo de Bombeiros resgatou o ouriço-cacheiro em Muriaé após o animal ser encontrado sobre o espelho de um banheiro e o devolveu ileso ao seu habitat natural.
articles.body:
Um ouriço-cacheiro foi resgatado dentro de um banheiro de uma casa, em Muriaé , na Zona da Mata, no domingo (1º) . O animal silvestre estava sobre um espelho quando o Corpo de Bombeiros chegou à residência para resgatá-lo.

Os moradores relataram à corporação que deixam as janelas da casa abertas com frequência e, apesar das grades de proteção, o ouriço pode ter passado entre elas . Apesar da suspeita, a forma como o animal entrou na casa não foi identificada.

Os bombeiros capturaram o ouriço, que não apresentava ferimentos ou sinais de lesão. Ele foi devolvido ao seu habitat natural, sem intercorrências.

Saiba o que fazer se encontrar um animal silvestre em casa

O Corpo de Bombeiros de Minas Gerais orienta que, ao encontrar um animal silvestre em casa, os moradores devem manter a calma e garantir que crianças e animais de estimação fiquem afastados .

O indicado é isolar o ambiente e evitar movimentos bruscos ou atitudes que possam assustar o animal. Se possível, portas ou janelas que permitam a saída esportânea do animal também devem ficar abertas.

O Corpo de Bombeiros deve ser acionado pelo 193 para avaliar a situação e, em casos necessários, fazer a captura do animal e direcioná-lo para seu ambiente natural.

“É importante ressaltar que animais silvestres não devem ser perseguidos, alimentados ou manuseados, pois, mesmo quando aparentemente inofensivos, podem reagir de maneira defensiva e provocar acidentes”, destaca a corporação, em nota.

articles.title: Preço da cesta básica sobe pelo 2º mês seguido e chega a quase R$ 3 mi | G1
articles.standfirst: Valor médio subiu R$ 47,91 e passou para R$ 2.994,93, puxado por cebola, tomate, mamão e carnes; Campos do Jordão segue tendo a cesta mais cara e Taubaté, a mais barata.
articles.summary: A cesta básica no Vale do Paraíba atingiu R$ 2.994 em outubro, impulsionada pela alta da carne bovina, da cebola e do tomate, superando a inflação oficial no período.
articles.body:
Preço da cesta básica sobe pelo 2º mês seguido e chega a R$ 2.994 em outubro no Vale do Paraíba — Foto: Valter Campanato / Agência Brasil

O preço da cesta básica no Vale do Paraíba subiu 1,63% em outubro de 2026, na comparação com setembro, e ficou mais caro pelo segundo mês consecutivo na região. Os dados são do levantamento divulgado nesta terça-feira (3) pelo Núcleo de Pesquisas Econômico-Sociais (Nupes), da Universidade de Taubaté (Unitau).

O valor médio da cesta passou de R$ 2.947,02 para R$ 2.994,93 — um acréscimo de R$ 47,91 no mês. Desse total, R$ 47,39 (98,9%) vieram apenas do grupo de alimentação, que representa 90,28% do peso total do índice. O levantamento considera uma cesta familiar com 44 produtos, destinada a uma família de cinco pessoas.

O novo avanço ocorre após a alta de 2,18% registrada em setembro, que havia interrompido duas quedas seguidas em julho e agosto. Somados, os aumentos de setembro (R$ 62,87) e outubro (R$ 47,91) totalizam R$ 110,78, revertendo integralmente o alívio de R$ 106,37 acumulado durante o inverno.

Campos do Jordão continua com a cesta mais cara da região, custando R$ 3.185,56, enquanto Taubaté mantém a mais barata, avaliada em R$ 2.904,31. A diferença entre os dois municípios chegou a R$ 281,25 (9,68%).

Segundo o Nupes, essa variação reflete fatores estruturais, como o custo logístico para subir a Serra da Mantiqueira até Campos do Jordão e a maior concorrência comercial às margens da Via Dutra em Taubaté .

Veja o valor e a variação mensal em cada cidade:

Caçapava : R$ 2.949,35 (+2,05% — maior alta percentual do mês)

São José dos Campos : R$ 2.940,51 (+1,46%)

Taubaté : R$ 2.904,31 (+1,39% — menor alta percentual do mês)

Chuvas e arroba do boi recorde puxam alta

De acordo com os economistas do Nupes, dois fatores principais pressionaram os preços em outubro:

Excesso de chuvas no Sudeste: O volume de chuva acima da média, iniciado em setembro, persistiu em outubro, prejudicando a colheita, o manejo no solo encharcado e a qualidade de hortaliças no interior paulista e no Triângulo Mineiro.

Disparada da carne bovina: Pela primeira vez, a arroba do boi gordo superou a marca de R$ 400 no mercado futuro da B3, impulsionada pela oferta restrita de animais prontos para abate (que teve queda de 12,11%), encarecendo cortes nobres nos supermercados.

Na média regional do Vale do Paraíba, os produtos que registraram as maiores altas em outubro foram:

🧅 Cebola: +20,54% (segunda alta seguida, após avançar 15,43% em setembro)

🍅 Tomate salada: +17,50% (subiu pelo 2º mês após disparar 45,34% em setembro)

🥬 Alface: +9,66% (solo encharcado comprometeu folhosas)

Já entre os itens que ficaram mais baratos na região estão:

🥕 Cenoura: -17,21% (4º mês seguido de queda, acumulando recuo de 48% devido ao alto estoque em São Gotardo-MG)

🥒 Abobrinha: -6,72% (devolveu parte da disparada de 56,06% registrada em setembro)

🧄 Alho: -6,30% (avanço da colheita da safra nacional no Cerrado ampliou a oferta)

Os três grupos que compõem a cesta tiveram alta em outubro: alimentação (+1,78%, passando para R$ 2.703,69), limpeza doméstica (+0,28%, a R$ 138,84) e higiene pessoal (+0,09%, a R$ 152,40).

articles.title: Western Sahara: Morocco celebrates end of the UN mission Minurso
articles.summary: An impasse between the US and Russia at the UN means its peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara has ended after 35 years.
articles.body:
Morocco has welcomed the end of a decades-long UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, after a diplomatic showdown between the US and Russia left the Security Council unable to agree on its future.

The council failed on Friday to renew the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (Minurso) after Russia vetoed a US-backed proposal. A rival Russian draft to extend the mission also failed to secure enough votes.

The decision raises questions about the future of Africa's longest territorial dispute and the fragile ceasefire between Morocco, which claims Western Sahara, and the Polisario Front which has been fighting for the territory's independence for more than 50 years.

Western Sahara, on Africa's north-west coast, was a Spanish colony until 1975. It has significant phosphate reserves and valuable fishing grounds along its Atlantic coast.

As Spain prepared to withdraw, both Morocco and Mauritania claimed the territory.

The International Court of Justice found historical ties of allegiance but no territorial sovereignty that overrode the Sahrawi people's right to self-determination.

Morocco's then King Hassan II responded by organising the Green March. On 6 November 1975 about 350,000 Moroccan civilians entered the territory in a mass demonstration intended to put pressure on Spain.

Days later, Spain signed the Madrid Accords with Morocco and Mauritania, agreeing to transfer administrative control. Morocco took the northern two-thirds and Mauritania the southern third. The agreement did not settle the question of sovereignty.

The Polisario Front, an independence movement founded in 1973, opposed the deal. It saw it as replacing Spanish colonial rule with Moroccan and Mauritanian control.

Mauritania renounced its claim in 1979, but Morocco continued fighting Polisario.

Algeria became Polisario's main regional ally, providing military support and hosting its leadership and thousands of Sahrawi refugees in camps near the city of Tindouf.

The North African country says its position is based on the right to self-determination, while Morocco sees Western Sahara as an integral part of its territory.

Morocco and Algeria fought a brief border war in 1963 over disagreements about territory inherited from French colonial rule. Their relationship has remained tense, with Western Sahara at the centre of their dispute.

After 16 years of fighting, Morocco and Polisario agreed to a UN-brokered ceasefire in 1991, with the territory divided by a sand wall, or berm, to keep the rival forces apart.

The UN established Minurso to monitor the ceasefire and organise a referendum on the territory's future. Sahrawis were meant to choose between independence and integration with Morocco.

The vote was scheduled for 1992 but never took place. The two sides could not agree on who would be eligible to participate, with disputes over voter identification becoming a major obstacle.

In 2007, Morocco put forward a proposal for autonomy, which would see Sahrawis managing their internal affairs, while Rabat retained control over defence and foreign relations.

The Polisario Front and Algeria rejected the plan, insisting on a referendum that included independence as an option.

Years of UN-sponsored negotiations failed to produce a breakthrough.

The ceasefire broke down in November 2020, when Polisario said it was resuming armed struggle.

But following a long diplomatic campaign by Morocco, the UN Security Council voted in 2025 in favour of a resolution backing the autonomy plan as the "most feasible" solution for the disputed territory.

While most Sahrawis live in the part of Western Sahara controlled by Morocco, tens of thousands are estimated to be in refugee camps in Algeria.

The US proposed extending Minurso's mandate for another year, but its draft went beyond the usual renewal.

It would have removed the word "referendum" from the mission's name and made Morocco's autonomy proposal the sole basis for further negotiations.

The draft received the support of 11 of the Security Council's 15 members, including France and the UK but Russia vetoed it, arguing that it was too favourable to Morocco.

Russia then proposed extending Minurso's mandate without changing its terms. That draft also failed, receiving only two votes in favour.

Minurso's mandate expired at the end of Saturday, 31 October. The UN said the following day that the mission had entered a liquidation period, with a reduced team overseeing the transfer of military equipment and other assets.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres said the Sahrawi people's right to self-determination must be respected and warned of the risk of renewed hostilities.

The Polisario Front condemned the US proposal. Its representative, Sidi Omar, thanked Russia for vetoing it, saying it would "torpedo the foundations of the UN peace process" and threaten regional and international peace.

Morocco, meanwhile, said the mission's personnel and equipment should leave the territory in the coming days, arguing that Western Sahara issue should no longer be considered by the Security Council.

Minurso had 155 military personnel and was expected to cost $62m (£46m) in the financial year beginning in June, according to a UN report.

Why is Morocco celebrating the end of the UN mission?

Morocco's royal palace welcomed the failure to renew Minurso's mandate.

In Laayoune, the territory's largest city, footage showed people celebrating, waving Moroccan flags and displaying portraits of King Mohammed VI.

"The decision is an opportunity for Rabat to challenge what it sees as an international mechanism that has failed to resolve the dispute," Issam Laaroussi, a Moroccan expert in international relations, tells the BBC.

He said Morocco would now have more room to push its autonomy proposal and shift negotiations away from a referendum on independence towards autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty.

The decision does not, however, change Western Sahara's legal status or amount to international recognition of Moroccan sovereignty.

Western Sahara remains on the UN list of non-self-governing territories, while the African Union officially recognises its independence, as the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR).

But the decision comes after several countries backed the position of Morocco, which in recent years has made securing international support for its claim a central part of its foreign policy.

In 2020, the US recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara as part of an agreement to establish diplomatic relations between Morocco and Israel.

France also backed Morocco's autonomy plan as the basis for resolving the dispute in 2024.

Morocco rejoined the African Union in 2017, more than three decades after leaving its predecessor, the Organisation of African Unity, in protest at the SADR's admission.

Since returning, Rabat has sought to build support for its position from within the organisation. At least 10 African countries have opened diplomatic missions in the territory in support of Rabat.

"Morocco is not necessarily seeking to abandon the UN process, but to change the framework for negotiations and draw greater support from regional organisations," says Laaroussi.

Addressing a special joint session of parliament on Monday, House of Representatives Speaker Ahmed Touizi hailed the end of Minurso as a victory for the country's diplomacy.

He said the country should now move from "managing the dispute to implementing its autonomy plan under Moroccan sovereignty, while pressing ahead with development projects in the territory."

The fear is that Minurso's departure could lead to renewed fighting.

The mission has monitored military developments and helped reduce the risk of escalation.

Aid organisation Oxfam warned that losing its monitoring and de-escalation role could undermine stability, with serious consequences for civilians.

Laaroussi admits that the mission's departure could create security gaps.

"Minurso's departure does not create the original conflict, because the conflict is already there, but it could aggravate an already fragile security environment," he says.

The UN decision has also fuelled nationalist rhetoric online.

Several Moroccan users have shared AI-generated images of themselves in military uniform, declaring their readiness to fight for Morocco's sovereignty over Western Sahara.

In Morocco, Western Sahara is widely regarded as a national cause. Political parties that are often divided on other issues are united in supporting the country's claim to sovereignty over the territory.

Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita has said the end of the mission does not mean the end of the ceasefire, and that Rabat remains committed to it "within respect of its security and sovereignty."

Polisario has not said what it will do next.

Any resumption of fighting could well draw in Algeria, as tensions with Morocco remain high.

According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), both countries significantly increased military spending last year, with SIPRI citing their dispute over Western Sahara as a key driver.

Algeria spent an estimated $25.4bn, more than four time Morocco's $6.3bn.

articles.title: 'Can't occupy a site for all times': SC on Delhi protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said no protest group can occupy a designated demonstration site indefinitely, observing that the right to protest
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said no protest group can occupy a designated demonstration site indefinitely, observing that the right to protest must be balanced with the rights of other citizens. Hearing pleas filed by traders' associations over the impact of demonstrations in Delhi, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said designated protest venues must be made available to different groups for specific periods."You can't occupy a site for all times. Where farmers, journalists, etc. will go? Everyone has right to protest. Designated time must be given for designated period," CJI Surya Kant said, according to LiveLaw.The bench also said that orders granting permission for protests must clearly specify the reasons for allowing or refusing them. "You can't prevent other people, that I am doing protest now you can't," the CJI observed.The court was hearing pleas raising concerns over alleged police brutality, mass detentions, the closure of Metro stations and internet shutdowns during protests, besides the impact of demonstrations on businesses.A traders' counsel told the court that around 50 lakh people lived in areas surrounding the protest site and claimed that shops remained shut, with virtually nobody visiting Connaught Place. The court issued notices to the Centre and other authorities on a plea by the Kirana Committee Delhi seeking a halt to protests during the festive season.However, the bench said it could not adjudicate the traders' grievances unless all organisations involved in the protests were made parties to the proceedings. It asked the traders' associations to implead the organisers of the anti-CEC protests.The hearing comes weeks after the Centre de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, identifying Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as alternative venues for demonstrations.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Surging ICE raids shadow final weeks of California congressional race
articles.summary: Local organisations and representatives say immigration raids have spread fear and uncertainty through communities.
articles.body:
Bakersfield, California – In a nondescript car park, a memorial with orange marigolds and prayer candles has been erected in honour of recently deceased labour organiser and civil rights leader Dolores Huerta.

Huerta was a well-known figure in California’s Central Valley, where she helped found the United Farm Workers union (UFW) and win better wages and working conditions for migrant and Latino labourers, who were vital to the state’s huge agricultural sector in the 1960s and 1970s.

The term “si, se puede”, coined by Huerta and translating to “yes, it can be done”, has also been placed on the display of a local theatre in her honour.

If Huerta represents a tradition of social and economic justice and labour organising that continues to resonate, an uptick in immigration raids across the valley over the last month has underscored the degree to which insecurity, both economic and political, remains a stubborn reality for many of the region’s agricultural workers.

Since early October, federal immigration agents, often masked and in unmarked vehicles, have fanned out across the Central Valley as part of a 45-day effort titled “Operation Save California” by the Trump administration.

Those raids, part of the administration’s mass deportation campaign, have become a flashpoint in the race for California’s 22nd congressional district, one of several contests in the state that Democrats hope will help deliver them a majority in the United States House of Representatives in the midterm elections on November 3.

While Republican incumbent David Valadao has been a fixture of the Central Valley for years, winning six of his last seven races, progressive challenger Randy Villegas is seeking to capitalise on popular frustration over the rising cost of living, healthcare cuts and immigration raids.

In a small building down the road from the Huerta memorial in Bakersfield, one day before the election, a room full of volunteers chant her slogan, encouraged by labour leaders and Democratic representatives such as California Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla, before they knock on doors.

“I’ve spoken to local business owners who have told me how their businesses are now struggling as a result of these ICE raids, and many of them have now pivoted to delivering things like groceries,” Villegas told Al Jazeera, noting that some residents are afraid of leaving their homes amid the increase in raids.

“It’s having an impact on people who just want to go to work, want to go to school,” he added.

Immigration authorities say the raids have targeted criminals and deny that they are racially discriminatory.

“Allegations that DHS law enforcement engages in ‘racial profiling’ are disgusting, reckless, and categorically FALSE,” the Department of Homeland Security said in an email. “What makes someone a target for immigration enforcement is if they are illegally in the US – NOT their skin colour, race, or ethnicity.”

But the administration’s depiction of targeted operations focused on people with serious criminal backgrounds is at odds with accounts from farmworkers, labour organisations, local officials, and advocacy groups, who describe aggressive methods and a dragnet approach.

“These are not criminals. These are hard-working, long-term members of our communities being unlawfully targeted simply for looking Latino and working class,” Teresa Romero, president of the UFW, whose members have campaigned for Villegas, said in a statement on October 10.

“We are seeing car windows being smashed and farm workers dragged from vehicles in the middle of the road while on their way to work.”

A woman who spoke with Al Jazeera over the phone on condition of anonymity said her husband, a farmworker in Fresno County, had been detained by immigration agents while returning home from work during the first week of October.

“I understand that if they [those arrested] are criminals or have done bad things, they have brought it on themselves,” the woman said of immigration arrests over a phone call. “But my husband has not done anything. The only thing he has done is work.”

She adds that her four children, all of whom are citizens born in the US, became anxious after the incident, and that some now begin to cry when they hear a knock at the door and fear that their mother will be taken away as well.

Local officials say such stories have reverberated through their communities.

“When you have a small community like ours, and folks are actually detained, word spreads,” said Olivia Calderon, mayor of the city of Arvin.

“I had pastors ask me whether ICE takes a day off on Sunday because people don’t want to go to church,” she added.

Villegas has drawn a link between the raids and Valadao’s vote in favour of a bill that is set to transform ICE, often accused of excessive force and disregard for civil liberties in its operations, into the most well-funded law enforcement agency in the country.

Asked about the impact of the raids in a debate with Villegas in early October, Valadao responded by mirroring the government’s claims that many of those targeted have criminal backgrounds and that “it is what it is.”

As Republicans and Democrats jostle for control of the House, the race has also received national attention.

Prominent figures such as leftist Senator Bernie Sanders, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson have visited in recent months to rally in support of their respective candidates.

Labour organisations, such as UFW, have also mobilised members to knock doors for Villegas.

But polls suggest a tight race between Valadao and Villegas, even after a partisan redistricting measure passed by California voters in 2025 resulted in a series of newly drawn maps, including parts of the 22nd district, meant to favour Democrats.

Valadao has proven himself to be a resilient candidate. His upbringing in the Central Valley, where his Portuguese parents settled and worked as dairy farmers, has helped him build close ties with ranchers, growers, and conservative voters who play an influential role in the region. While California in general is a bastion of support for the Democratic Party, rural areas are often favourable terrain for Republicans.

While Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris defeated Donald Trump in California by nearly 20 points in 2024, Trump carried Kern County, where Bakersfield is located, by a similar margin.

Still, Villegas and his supporters are hoping that concerns over the rising cost of living, driven in part by the Trump administration’s decision to launch a war on Iran that has sent energy prices soaring, will help him dislodge the resilient Republican incumbent.

Priscilla Ortega, a 23-year-old in the city of Lamont, said she is “annoyed and very angry” about rising prices and the impact of immigration raids.

“It was really unnecessary,” she said of the war on Iran, adding that rising fuel costs have made her commute to her job as a warehouse worker in the region much more expensive.

“That could have gone to food for my household or bills that need to be paid,” she added. “People are sick of the prices increasing.”

articles.title: Lebanon cuts power to public bodies as electricity crisis deepens
articles.summary: Political disputes and war worsen Lebanon’s electricity crisis, as experts say deeper reforms are necessary.
articles.body:
Beirut, Lebanon – Lebanon’s Ministry of Energy and Water has begun shutting down the supply of electricity to approximately 100 public institutions that have outstanding bill payments, according to local media.

The decision, which began to take effect on Monday, marks a further escalation in Energy Minister Joe Saddi’s dispute with the government. Saddi recently began boycotting cabinet meetings over what he claims is the government’s failure to address his demands to increase power supply, reduce the burden of fuel costs and settle unpaid bills to the state-owned electricity company.

Lebanon has struggled with power cuts for years , but state-provided electricity dropped sharply following the 2019 economic and banking crisis. In Beirut, for example, electricity supplied by the state was once available for about 21 hours a day, but that has dropped in recent years to just two to four hours, with some days seeing no power at all.

Analysts say that deep structural issues are behind the Lebanese state’s failure to provide electricity in recent years and without deep reform, little is likely to change.

“The key problem in the power sector is, as everyone knows, that we have a lot of corruption,” said Jessica Obeid, a Lebanese energy expert. “This sector has corruption across the entire supply chain, and it’s in the billions of dollars, so it is not something that is going to disappear overnight.”

In place of a reliable state-provided electricity supply, an alternative economy has emerged where locals rely on private generators, many of which are run by political parties or individuals with close ties to power .

When a government led by reformists took control in early 2025, there was hope that the situation would improve. But more than a year and a half later, state electricity supplies are still meagre, while energy costs and inflation have skyrocketed.

The World Bank projects that year-on-year inflation in Lebanon will be 17.5 percent this year, while fuel costs connected to the United States-Israel war on Iran have meant electricity costs for fuel-guzzling private generators have increased exponentially for many in Lebanon.

“We rely on very expensive diesel, and [state-owned] power plants are very old. All of that means that we cannot be looking for band-aid solutions,” Obeid said. “What the sector is mostly lacking is a vision of what kind of power system we want in this country.”

The dispute over electricity has heightened speculation about a possible cabinet reshuffle and the resignation of Saddi, who is a member of the right-wing Lebanese Forces (LF) party. For his part, Saddi told Lebanese media that he had been pushing the government of Prime Minister Nawaf Salam to prioritise his ministry’s portfolio earlier this year, but had stopped applying as much pressure when Israel’s war on Lebanon intensified in early March.

After the draft 2027 budget was announced in October, the LF and Saddi raised objections, claiming not enough attention was being given to the electricity sector.

And in recent weeks, Saddi has stepped up his efforts to draw attention to the needs of his ministry. In early October, he pledged to start boycotting cabinet meetings. Last Thursday, Saddi was joined in boycotting a cabinet meeting by three ministerial colleagues from his LF party. Saddi said this is a way to pressure the government to give adequate attention and focus to the country’s ongoing electricity crisis.

Sami Zoughaib, an economist and research manager at The Policy Initiative, a Lebanese think tank, told Al Jazeera that the boycott was a political move by Saddi and his party to try and avoid losing popular support.

“If they fail in the eyes of people, it would be very difficult for them to have the ministry again,” Zoughaib said.

Under previous Lebanese governments, the Energy Ministry was at times managed by the LF’s main Christian rival, the Free Patriotic Movement (FPM). In recent months, the FPM’s leader Gebran Bassil has criticised Saddi’s management of the ministry. Bassil himself is a former energy minister who failed to deliver on his own promises of increasing Lebanon’s state-electricity provision to 24 hours a day.

With the electricity crisis ongoing, Qatar has stepped in to provide a lifeline to the Lebanese state. Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani visited Beirut last month and confirmed plans for an energy partnership, including a solar power project . the Reuters news agency subsequently reported that Doha has offered to build two power plants over the next three years and to supply the country with a 20-year liquefied natural gas supply deal.

Should the deal be approved, it would be a boon to Lebanon’s energy sector. But analysts believe the electricity sector still needs structural reforms for it to meet residents’ needs, including potentially rebuilding the entire grid.

Zoughaib said that the aged energy infrastructure in Lebanon meant the pre-2019 model of providing state-subsidised electricity ate up a significant portion of the government’s yearly budget.

“The state cannot reproduce the model of the past,” he said. “It definitely doesn’t have the money. The way to do it is to reform the entire sector and to try to create a new scenario whereby a sustainable solution is possible.”

Saddi has previously proposed bringing in private investors to run public-private partnerships to solve Lebanon’s energy crisis, a strategy that has become common around the world.

But experts said Lebanon’s lack of stability – suffering through repeated Israeli attacks with the potential for more to come – would deter investors. The country’s failure to reform its financial and banking sectors, seven years after the onset of its economic crisis, would pose another major obstacle.

“When we look for investors who will make that investment, political stability is a key thing of course,” Obeid, the energy expert, said. “Secondly, this is a bankrupt country that has been bankrupt for at least seven years, and nobody has done anything about it, so it does not show any actual will for reform and increases risks [for investment].”

Additionally, she said, Lebanon’s grid is damaged and requires rehabilitation. Experts said that government after government have looked for unsustainable short-term fixes and not had the political will to do more than go after political wins.

“The problem I have in Lebanon is everything is presented as if we are inventing electricity,” Obeid said. “The year is 2026, almost 2027. Lebanon is a very small country. It just needs a vision and someone to take the bold decisions.”

articles.title: At least 73 injured as Russia bombs Ukrainian hospital and power plants
articles.summary: Medical facility was struck by Russian ballistic missiles and aerial bombs overnight.
articles.body:
Russia has bombed a hospital in Kharkiv, injuring at least 73 people, while also carrying out several attacks on energy infrastructure across multiple Ukrainian regions.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on X that “the Russians directly struck a city clinical hospital. Seventy-three people were injured, and the cardiology department, where people were receiving treatment, was damaged.”

Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov confirmed on Telegram that the hospital sustained heavy damage in Monday night’s bombardment, with more than 1,000 windows shattered.

Separately, Ukrainian energy sites were hit, including in Kharkiv, in what President Zelenskyy described as a “complex, massive attack”.

“The main target was energy – power generation facilities and substations – in the Odesa, Cherkasy, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Kharkiv, Dnipro, Chernivtsi, Chernihiv, and Rivne regions,” he said in a post on X.

Zelenskyy added that Russia had launched 289 attack drones overnight, as well as 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles. This comes a day after at least 33 people were killed in a Russian strike on an aid distribution centre.

The UN’s human rights mission in Ukraine on Tuesday slammed the deadly attack, saying it likely violated international law.

“The timing and location of the humanitarian distribution was well publicised,” Danielle Bell, the head of the rights mission, said.

“Either the Russian armed forces knew that there was a humanitarian distribution taking place, or they failed to take the most basic steps to find out what was happening in this village they were planning to attack,” Bell added.

Meanwhile, the Russian Ministry of Defence said it had targeted electricity facilities in the Vinnytsia, ⁠Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regions. In its statement, it said the sites supplied power to the Ukrainian army and military factories.

More than 180,000 people were without power in the Zhytomyr ⁠region on Tuesday morning after Russian attacks, Governor Vitalii Bunechko said. Odesa has implemented scheduled power outages in response to the attacks.

Meanwhile, two employees at a Russian oil refinery in Yaroslavl were injured during a Ukrainian drone attack that caused a fire at the site, according to Governor Mikhail Yevrayev.

The latest exchange of attacks comes as the United States ramps up efforts to end the war, with a meeting between US, Russian and Ukrainian officials due to take place in Abu Dhabi next week. US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff said in a post on X late on Monday that the discussions would focus on “post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts, and next steps toward peace”.

Witkoff added that US negotiators would meet with representatives from France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the European Union and NATO in Brussels this week. He said the talks would focus on security guarantees for Ukraine, Europe’s post-war security architecture and economic opportunities to support Ukraine’s reconstruction.

This comes as global attention turns to Tuesday’s midterm elections in the US. Reporting from Kyiv, Al Jazeera’s Audrey MacAlpine said these were arguably the most important elections in recent years for Ukrainians.

“Since the Trump administration took office and the House and Senate flipped Republican, there have been no significant military aid packages for Ukraine. In comparison, Biden, during the early years of the war, you were looking at $60b in military aid for Ukraine,” MacAlpine said.

“Europe has largely filled that gap but certainly Ukraine would like to resume that aid from the US. That’s been at the top of President Zelenskyy’s agenda for over six months now,” she added.

articles.title: Deadly RSF drone attacks reveal deep divisions between Sudan and Ethiopia
articles.summary: Sudan demands UN accountability after devastating drone attacks expose a complex regional crisis.
articles.body:
The Sudanese government’s allegations that Ethiopia is behind a deadly wave of unmanned aerial assaults belie a deep and longstanding rift between the two countries, which threatens to intensify internal conflicts in both.

Sudan has officially lodged complaints with the United Nations Security Council and the African Union’s Peace and Security Council over allegations that the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary – which has been at war with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) since April 2023 – is using Ethiopian territory to launch attacks against civilian sites, including power stations.

Ethiopia’s alleged support for the RSF has triggered differences within the SAF on how to respond next, Sudanese border affairs specialist Abdul Kareem Al-Almin Ahmed told Al Jazeera.

“The mutual accusations are many and almost daily, and the tension on the part of the Sudanese army has reached high levels, to the degree that made some voices inside the Sudanese army and the forces allied with it demand that Sudan declare war on Ethiopia based on these interventions,” Al-Almin told Al Jazeera.

Suspected RSF drone attacks have heavily damaged civilian infrastructure in SAF-controlled areas. More than 90 percent of power stations in Sudanese cities have been rendered out of service due to drone attacks, and al-Almin said the technological capabilities of these weapons indicate significant external backing.

“They are mysterious drones, drones that reach long distances, and almost all Sudanese lands are currently violated by these drones, which confirms that they are drones with a special characteristic and flight properties for a long range and have high destructive power,” Al-Almin added.

A detailed report prepared by the Sudanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs alongside military intelligence claimed that 70 separate assaults involving 187 one-way attack drones were launched from Ethiopian territory between February and October. The frequency of these attacks seems to be increasing, with 28 attacks carried out by 97 drones in October.

The use of armed drones has been catastrophic for civilians in Sudan, with 13 million people already displaced and thousands at risk of famine due to the war.

Between February 15 and October 27, drone attacks killed 176 Sudanese soldiers and 484 civilians, according to a report compiled by the Transitional Sovereignty Council, which is linked to the de facto Sudanese leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and the SAF. It identified Asosa Airport in western Ethiopia, the Kurmuk-Gizen border area, and the Bahir Dar airbase in Amhara as specific launch sites for drone attacks.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said on Saturday he was appalled by the use of drones in the war and condemned the catastrophic toll this was having on civilians. A drone attack on displaced families in Wad el-Mahi , near the Ethiopian border on October 3, killed 26 women and four children. Another drone attack in Nyala, in Sudan’s Darfur region, on October 26 killed at least 21 people and injured at least 40.

The Sudanese military has repeatedly accused the Ethiopian government of aiding the RSF. Addis Ababa denies the claims and has in turn accused the Sudanese government of backing rebels linked to the Tigray People’s Liberation Front .

The tensions between Sudan and Ethiopia extend beyond these drone attacks and allegations of support for rebel groups. They also involve a confrontation over water resources and strategic regional alliances.

There have been ongoing tensions between Sudan and Ethiopia over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), built by Addis Ababa on the Nile River.

Egypt and Sudan rely heavily on the Nile for water supplies and, being downstream, fear the GERD threatens their national security and claim it breaches international law.

“The Sudanese-Ethiopian file is a complex file, in which many factors have intertwined: The Renaissance Dam problem first … and the rapprochement between the Sudanese army and the Egyptian government,” Al-Almin said. The Sudanese government is also angered that the RSF is allegedly receiving support from Ethiopia, he added.

But Badr Hassan Al-Shafei, a professor of African studies and conflict resolution expert, said fears of an escalation that could harm Sudan and Ethiopia are preventing an all-out confrontation between the two countries.

In a study published by the Al Jazeera Centre for Studies, Al-Shafei wrote that “Khartoum’s interest lies in the stability of its eastern neighbourhood to avoid security threats and waves of asylum.

“Khartoum fears that providing military support to Tigray will lead to an explosion of the situation on its borders, which may increase displacement operations that the border Sudanese states cannot bear, especially in light of the continuation of the war against Hemedti,” Al-Shafei stated.

A direct military confrontation with Addis Ababa would severely strain an already exhausted Sudanese military apparatus, which is still involved in intense battles with the RSF in the southeast of the country.

Ultimately, leaders of both countries recognise the catastrophic potential of expanding the battlefield beyond each other’s borders.

“If the Sudanese army opens a war front with Ethiopia, this is not in its favour and confuses the region,” Al-Amin wrote.

“[Sudan could find itself] fighting on two fronts: Fighting the Rapid Support Forces that occupy part of Sudan, and fighting the Ethiopian army that possesses its capabilities and the border extension capable of reaching through it.”

articles.title: Floods and severe weather beset parts of the U.S. on Election Day
articles.summary: Flash flooding, heavy rainfall and tornadoes have forced election officials in three different regions across the United States to move polling locations, scrambling Election Day plans in hot-button races.
articles.body: Flash flooding, heavy rainfall and tornadoes have forced election officials in three different regions across the United States to move polling locations, scrambling Election Day plans in hot-button races. At least 21 polling locations were moved across eight Florida counties — including Brevard, Broward, Highlands, Indian River, Martin, Okeechobee, Palm Beach and St. Lucie counties — after intense rainfall caused flash floods Monday and into Tuesday morning. Roads were impassable in several parts of the state’s Atlantic coast after a storm dumped as much as 22 inches of rain in 24 hours in a storm that “exceeded everyone’s expectations,” as one forecaster put it. Severe storms were moving across Oklahoma, Texas and Arkansas overnight. Forecasters issued a tornado watch that lasted until about 2:45 a.m. local time Tuesday. Forecasters were also predicting possible flash flooding in parts of Alabama, Tennessee, Arkansas and Mississippi on Tuesday, as that storm system continued to travel east. A flood watch remained in effect in some parts of Florida, though rainfall rates were slowing. “Areas affected by catastrophic flooding remain extremely sensitive to any additional rainfall,” forecasters wrote in a Tuesday morning discussion. In Oklahoma, a tornado Sunday forced Cimarron County officials to change one of its polling locations. The tornado, which had peak winds of about 100 mph, snapped tree branches, damaged the roof of the Keyes Community Center and collapsed a wall, according to a damage survey report from the National Weather Service. Follow live updates on the midterm elections In an emergency request, county election officials said the tornado caused “considerable structural damage” to the community center “rendering the polling location unsafe.” And after historic flooding in the Four Corners region, Utah Lt. Gov. Deidre M. Henderson declared a state of emergency and issued a special accommodation that will allow voters registered in San Juan County who are isolated by floodwaters to request and return ballots electronically. The Colorado secretary of state is allowing a similar measure for voters — allowing votes online — in La Plata and Archuleta counties, according to 9 News. More election day surprises could be in store. Experts say inclement weather has suppressed voter turnout in past elections. In research of elections from 1948 to 2000, researchers observed a modest drop in turnout during unusually intense rain storms. “What we found was that for every inch of rain that a county received above its average amount of rainfall, voter turnout went down about eight-tenths of 1 percentage point,” said Brad Gomez, an associate professor of political science at Florida State University. But experts said the effect of rain on turnout is diminishing over time as more people choose to vote early or vote by mail, and they said it’s hard to predict what effect the inclement weather will have, if any, on key races. In Florida, Gov. Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency in seven counties along the Atlantic seaboard that are being hit with flash flooding and extreme precipitation. Damage in parts of Colorado remains widespread after heavy rain and flooding, with first responders searching for people who may be stranded across the area, including by helicopter. People with homes along the Animas River in southwestern Colorado were also facing evacuation. Record rainfall was also reported in usually dry Arizona, causing deadly flooding and power outages. The brief closure of two voting centers in Maricopa County sparked a chorus of conspiracy insinuations online Monday. Two out of the 254 polling locations in the county had to be temporarily shuttered “due to power related issues,” election authorities announced on social media. The two polling locations have since been reopened, authorities said, but some online used the shutdown to allege impropriety in the competitive swing state. Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs issued a statewide emergency declaration Monday after recently issuing an emergency for Navajo and Coconino counties. The governors of New Mexico and Colorado also asked President Donald Trump to declare a major disaster to receive federal funding assistance. Rain is also expected to hit the central U.S. as voters head to the polls there Tuesday, but experts said the impact on the election outcome is expected to be minimal. The weather’s effect on voter turnout will be watched closely by campaigns seeking to draw as many supporters as possible to polling places. The storm system will move east Tuesday, with heavy rain possible in Mississippi, Missouri and western Tennessee. On Election Day, “scattered flash floods are possible” in the lower Mississippi River valley and into areas such as Memphis, Tennessee, said Jennifer Tate, a meteorologist with the weather service’s Weather Prediction Center in College Park, Maryland. Much of the rest of the central U.S. — from east Texas to the Midwest — can expect wet, dreary weather on Election Day. Election Day weather on the West Coast looks mostly pleasant, with pockets of rain in Northern California. Outside of Florida, the East Coast looks clear, though some rain is expected in Maine.

articles.title: Proposal for free bus service in Guernsey scrapped
articles.summary: The one-year free bus service pilot was initially put forward as an amendment to next year's budget.
articles.body:
Proposals for a free bus service in Guernsey will no longer be considered for next year's budget, deputies who suggested the move have said.

Deputies Sally Rochester and Ross Le Brun put the plan forward as an amendment to the 2027 budget , asking the Policy and Resources Committee for £1.9m to "enable the existing public transport service" to be made free of charge in a one-year pilot.

They have now pulled the plans after "concern from [operator] Stagecoach" that increased passenger numbers could mean certain routes not coping with the additional demand.

Rochester said she and Le Brun were committed to working with the Environment and Infrastructure Committee to explore plans for the future.

Rochester also acknowledged the pilot would not be possible if buses were "at capacity".

Speaking to BBC Radio Guernsey, she said: "This amendment was all about supporting those in our community that are facing cost of living challenges.

"It was about delivering the transport strategy so you could have access to a free bus service - make their lives easier, make their lives better.

"Now we're not going to be able to do that if the bus service is at capacity."

She said the "logical conclusion is that we would need more buses" while Stagecoach's contract "would need to be expanded" to provide the additional capacity.

Rochester said these elements are "what we'll be looking into and hopefully bringing this back some time in the future".

A spokesperson for Stagecoach said it welcomed "any initiative that encourages more people to use public transport and recognise the potential benefits of making bus travel more accessible".

But it said it was important that "any proposal to introduce free bus travel is carefully considered to ensure that sufficient capacity is available across the network to accommodate the additional passenger demand such a scheme could generate".

The company added: "Our priority is to ensure that bus services remain reliable, accessible and able to meet the needs of all passengers, particularly on routes that already experience high levels of demand."

The proposal was one of 30 changes put forward to next year's budget, scheduled for consideration on Tuesday.

Other amendments put forward include efforts to secure money for States' committees faced with budget cuts, attempts to freeze fuel duty and cuts to overseas aid.

articles.title: At least 33 dead after Russia drops nine bombs on a Ukrainian school building
articles.summary: Dozens of people were killed when Russia dropped at least nine bombs on a school building in southeastern Ukraine where they had taken shelter, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, describing it as “one of the deadliest attacks of this war.”
articles.body: Dozens of people were killed when Russia dropped at least nine bombs on a school building in southeastern Ukraine where they had taken shelter, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, describing it as “one of the deadliest attacks of this war.” At least 33 people have been confirmed dead and another 50 are still unaccounted for after the attack on the building in Komyshuvakha in the Zaporizhzhia region, which local governor Mykhailo Semikin said was being used as a shelter and a humanitarian aid distribution center. Semikin said they were in a newly-built, EU-funded reinforced basement designed to withstand most strikes, but the massive force of the bombs caused the concrete structure to collapse and a fire broke out. The shelter was built last year in an effort to keep classes going during wartime, but many civilians have since left as the fighting got closer to the village, and it is not currently used as a school. Instead, local authorities are using it as an administrative center and humanitarian hub. The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine highlighted in a statement on Tuesday that the attack took place just as civilians from the area gathered to receive humanitarian aid. “The timing and location of the humanitarian distribution was well publicized,” said Danielle Bell, the head of the mission. “Either the Russian armed forces knew that there was a humanitarian distribution taking place, or they failed to take the most basic steps to find out what was happening in this village they were planning to attack. In either case, this attack seems to have violated the most fundamental principles of international humanitarian law.” Zelensky said the attack came just before Russia launched another massive barrage of hundreds of drones and dozens of powerful cruise and ballistic missiles targeting Ukraine’s energy infrastructure – despite US President Donald Trump’s repeated calls for energy ceasefire. “It is very telling that all of this is happening on the day of the US congressional elections. The Russians believe that America will not notice this signal from them. But such terror must be noticed and stopped,” Zelensky said on Tuesday morning. “Ukraine must be helped to defend its skies, otherwise Russia will never stop its missile strikes. It is essential to help build peace honestly and reliably, and America can do that,” Zelensky added. The latest attacks by Russia come amid a renewed push for negotiations by the Trump administration. US envoy Steve Witkoff recently held a meeting with Zelensky in Norway before flying to St. Petersburg to meet with the Russian President Vladimir Putin. Separately, first lady Melania Trump helped to secure a ceasefire in the occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, which enabled the evacuation of hundreds of civilians over the weekend. Trump’s office announced on Tuesday that the first lady would bring together representatives from Russia and Ukraine at the White House on Thursday, calling it “an extraordinary moment in American history.” Double-tap strike The strike on Monday is among the deadliest since the start of the war, but the past few months have been exceptionally bloody for Ukrainian civilians. Russia ramped up its aerial attacks on towns and cities across the country over the summer, striking at all times of the day. At least 33 people were killed last month when Russia hit two civilian buses in Kramatorsk in the Donetsk region. In August, 38 people were killed when a Russian drone strike on an ammunition depot near the capital triggered a large fire and multiple explosions that lasted hours in a residential area near Kyiv. And a mass Russian missile attack on Kyiv in July killed 33 people across the city in a coordinated barrage. The assault against Komyshuvakha on Monday followed a familiar scenario in which Russian forces launch the first wave of strikes, wait for emergency services to arrive and then strike again. At least two first responders, named locally as Denys Konovalenko and Oleksiy Sushchevsky, both 44, were killed after rushing to the scene of the first strike. The Ukrainian Police said at least four of its officers have also been killed in the attack. They were named as Mykhailo Buzhenko and Mykola Balanda, both of who had more than two decades of police service under their belts, and Mykhailo Romanov and Dmytro Besedin, both of whom have been community police officers for more than a decade. “(They) were helping local residents take shelter in an underground school. A treacherous follow-up strike trapped everyone who was trying to escape,” the police said in a statement. Semikin told Ukraine’s national TV broadcast on Tuesday that Russia used KAB-500 and FAB-3000 bombs in the attack. “To put this into perspective, this is a three-ton aerial bomb containing nearly 1.5 tons of explosive material; such weapons are primarily designed to destroy heavy concrete fortifications and bunkers,” he said.
