articles.title: Melania Trump hosting Ukraine, Russia representatives at White House
articles.summary: First lady Melania Trump will be hosting representatives from Russia and Ukraine at the White House, according to a Tuesday press release. The announcement comes after the first lady secured a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the front-line city of Oleshky earlier this month. “First Lady Melania Trump will personally bring representatives of…
articles.body:
First lady Melania Trump will be hosting representatives from Russia and Ukraine at the White House, according to a Tuesday press release.

The announcement comes after the first lady secured a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the front-line city of Oleshky earlier this month.

“First Lady Melania Trump will personally bring representatives of Russia and Ukraine, two nations actively at war, together at the White House,” the release said. “This event represents an extraordinary moment in American history.”

The first lady is also scheduled to deliver remarks on the Oleshky ceasefire on Thursday at the White House, per the release.

The temporary pause in conflict , which started at 3 a.m. local time on Oct. 27, was set to last through Oct. 31 to allow for the delivery of humanitarian aid. It was originally set to begin on Oct. 29.

In a statement posted to the social platform X on Oct. 27, the first lady said, “timing was accelerated two days ahead of schedule to protect the safety of civilians and to facilitate the delivery of critical humanitarian aid.”

“The ceasefire’s geographic area has expanded beyond Oleshky, within the Kherson Region, to provide safe passage for the humanitarian convoys,” she added.

Oleshky is in Ukraine’s southern Kherson Oblast on the east bank of the Dnieper River. The city had a prewar population of around 24,000 people and was pulled to the front line after Ukraine liberated western Kherson Oblast in November 2022, according to a report from the Institute for the Study of War . About 2,000 people remained in the city following population displacement and evacuation.

In an earlier press release announcing the ceasefire, the first lady said, “the situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky’s remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water.”

“It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible,” she added.

Earlier in October, Pope Leo XIV urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in a phone call to cooperate with Russia to allow humanitarian aid into Oleshky.

articles.title: MICHAEL RUIZ: Mangione’s new argument to escape NY murder case: Same gun, same killing, same prosecution
articles.summary: Luigi Mangione's lawyers argue murder and federal stalking charges target the same evil, pressing a double jeopardy defense to dismiss New York charges.
articles.body: Luigi Mangione's lawyers are doubling down on their double jeopardy defense in their fight to have the admitted assassin spared from New York murder charges after admitting to what they say was essentially the same crime in federal court. Murder is the same evil as stalking with intent to kill — and then killing, they argued. The claims came in response to Manhattan prosecutors who have asked a New York judge to reject his bid to drop his state-level charges following a federal guilty plea in which he admitted to assassinating UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, a 50-year-old father of two who Mangione shot in the back outside a Hilton hotel in the middle of the Big Apple. BRAVE WIDOW OF SLAIN UNITEDHEALTHCARE CEO BRIAN THOMPSON COMES FACE TO FACE WITH LUIGI MANGIONE FOR FIRST TIME Prosecutors have said that since Mangione was not prosecuted for federal firearms offenses, there is no double jeopardy if the state level ones remain on the table. They argued that the murder charges should still go forward because although Mangione admitted to killing Thompson, that's not the same "harm or evil" involved in the federal stalking charges. And they argued that even though Mangione withdrew a potential "extreme emotional disturbance" defense specific to Empire State law, that doesn't mean the federal case prevented him from using it. Mangione's lawyers, Karen Friedman Agnifilo, Marc Agnifilo and Jacob Kaplan, attacked all three arguments in a reply made public over the weekend. LUIGI MANGIONE PLEA BUZZ RAISES POTENTIAL PAUL MANAFORT PROBLEM FOR PROSECUTORS READ the defense reply: First, they argued that although the federal firearms charges were dismissed, he was still "prosecuted" for them, putting him at risk of double jeopardy. "The statutory definition of being 'prosecuted' for an offense does not require that the defendant plead guilty to that specific offense," Mangione's lawyers wrote. LUIGI MANGIONE HEARING SET FOR FRIDAY STIRS PLEA DEAL SPECULATION IN HIS FEDERAL CASE Their client pleaded guilty to two federal charges, although he'd initially faced more. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X "In other words, when Mangione pleaded guilty to the federal indictment, the criminal action in which he had been charged with possession and use of the firearm was terminated for statutory double jeopardy purposes," they wrote. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS They also argued that stalking Thompson with intent to kill him is the same "core misconduct" as murdering him. In order to get around New York's double jeopardy law, which is more restrictive than the U.S. Constitution, prosecutors need to show that the state charges are meant to prevent different "harms or evils" than the federal ones he already pleaded guilty to. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB "One of the harms clearly addressed by the expansive federal stalking statute is stalking with the intent to kill and resulting in the killing of the person stalked," Mangione's lawyers wrote. "It is a statute that, like a state murder statute, is intended to keep people safe from being murdered — the oldest crime there is." LUIGI MANGIONE'S TEAM FIRES BACK AT PLEA DEAL REPORT, CALLS LEAKS THREAT TO FAIR TRIAL They argued that while the federal stalking charge includes other elements, including interstate travel and the use of electronic communications, they are "not related" to the core evil of the crime, which is killing someone. "The federal government does have an interest, however, in preventing people from [traveling] or using electronics as part of the crime of killing another person, or intending to do so. That is what makes the stalking statute similar to the murder statute in terms of the evils or harms both are looking to prevent."
